stories.headline: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize as US imposes sanctions on International Criminal Court
stories.body:
South African judge Navi Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

The Trump administration announced sanctions targeting the International Criminal Court as an institution. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the sanctions ban US entities from financial transactions with the court. Rubio warned that either the court ends its threats or the US will end the court. The court was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide. It currently has 125 member states. But the United States, Russia, China, India, and Israel are not member states.

The United States gave a six-month grace period before certain sanctions take effect. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the US decision a serious blow to collective criminal justice. He said the court is a key pillar of that justice. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions. Netanyahu called the court a political body that threatens democratic sovereignty.

claims.text: South African judge Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.
The Trump administration announced sanctions targeting the International Criminal Court as an institution.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the sanctions include a ban on US entities making financial transactions with the International Criminal Court.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned, "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC."
The International Criminal Court was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide, and has 125 member states.
The United States, Russia, China, India, and Israel are not member states of the International Criminal Court.
The United States provided a six-month grace period before certain sanctions on the International Criminal Court take effect.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar".
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed the US sanctions, describing the International Criminal Court as a political body that threatens democratic sovereignty.

stories.headline: US agrees deal with Russia to import diesel despite opposition from Ukraine and lawmakers
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Moscow to supply diesel to global markets. The deal permits Russia to sell diesel to the United States and other countries.

The US Treasury Department issued a temporary licence to support the agreement. The licence suspends sanctions on Russian diesel exports through April 7, 2027. Russia will supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately. It will supply 500,000 tonnes in November. Moscow will then export 1 million tonnes shortly after. It is scheduled to export another 3 million tonnes depending on refinery conditions.

President Donald Trump reached the diesel agreement during a phone call with Vladimir Putin. The two leaders originally scheduled the call to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia.

Fuel prices in the United States were high before the deal. The average price of diesel in the US stood at $6.28 per gallon at the time of the announcement. That price was down from a record $6.53 per gallon in late September. Average regular gasoline prices in the US rose more than 46 percent since late February to reach $4.37 per gallon. US diesel prices increased 67 percent over the same time frame.

Russia faced production problems before the agreement. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries caused Russia's diesel production to fall by an estimated 30 percent.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the new agreement. Zelenskyy said that easing sanctions on Russian energy plays into Moscow's hands. He said the move prolongs the war.

American politicians also criticized the move. Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen condemned President Donald Trump for lifting sanctions on Russian fossil fuels. Several Republican lawmakers also condemned Trump for lifting the sanctions.

claims.text: US President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to supply diesel to the US and global markets.
The US Treasury Department issued a temporary licence suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports through April 7, 2027.

Under the agreement, Russia is scheduled to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, 500,000 tonnes in November, 1 million tonnes shortly after, and another 3 million tonnes depending on refinery conditions.
President Donald Trump reached the diesel agreement during a phone call with Vladimir Putin originally scheduled to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia.
The average price of diesel in the United States stood at $6.28 per gallon at the time of the announcement, down from a record $6.53 per gallon in late September.
Average regular gasoline prices in the United States rose more than 46 percent since late February to $4.37 per gallon, while diesel prices increased 67 percent over the same period.
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries caused Russia's diesel production to fall by an estimated 30 percent.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the deal, stating that easing sanctions on Russian energy plays into Moscow's hands and prolongs the war.
Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen and several Republican lawmakers condemned President Donald Trump for lifting sanctions on Russian fossil fuels.

stories.headline: Strong earthquake hits Panama causing infrastructure damage and economic losses
stories.body:
A 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck Panama near the community of Pitaloza Arriba. The US Geological Survey also registered the main earthquake at magnitude 7.7 at a depth of 12.6 kilometers. It was the strongest quake in that part of Panama since at least 1951.

Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino appealed for calm after the earthquake. Mulino wrote on X that what happened should not generate alarm and disorder. Preliminary estimates from the US Geological Survey show economic losses in Panama will likely exceed $1 billion.

The quake caused structural collapses and damage in Penonomé. Damaged sites include the St John Baptist Cathedral, the governor's office building, and the Dos Continentes hotel. Panama's Ministry of Education ordered schools across the country to close.

Transportation was disrupted in several areas. Tocumen International Airport in Panama City temporarily suspended flights and evacuated facilities for safety checks. Panama City's Metro system halted service on lines 1 and 2 as a precaution. But the Panama Canal Authority confirmed ship traffic continued normally.

Earlier in 2026, twin earthquakes in Venezuela killed at least 6,500 people in June. A magnitude 7.4 quake in Colombia killed at least 289 people in August.

claims.text: A 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck Panama, centered near the community of Pitaloza Arriba, according to the US Geological Survey.
The US Geological Survey registered the main earthquake at magnitude 7.7 at a depth of 12.6 kilometers, making it the strongest quake in that part of Panama since at least 1951.
Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino appealed for calm following the earthquake, stating on X, "What happened should not be used to generate alarm and disorder."
Preliminary estimates from the US Geological Survey indicate that economic losses in Panama from the earthquake are likely to exceed $1 billion.
The earthquake caused structural collapses and damage in Penonomé, including at the St John Baptist Cathedral, the governor's office building, and the Dos Continentes hotel.
Panama's Ministry of Education ordered schools across the country to close following the earthquake.
Tocumen International Airport in Panama City temporarily suspended flight operations and evacuated facilities to conduct safety checks.
Panama City's Metro system temporarily halted service on lines 1 and 2 as a precaution after the quake.
The Panama Canal Authority confirmed that ship traffic and operations along the canal continued normally following the earthquake.
Twin earthquakes in northern Venezuela killed at least 6,500 people in June 2026, while a magnitude 7.4 quake in Colombia killed at least 289 people in August 2026.

stories.headline: Delhi authorities deploy heavy security and restrict transit ahead of opposition protest
stories.body:
The Cockroach Janta Party called on supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10, 2026. The group released a poster demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They also demanded the rollback of the Special Intensive Revision.

Delhi Police denied permission for the planned protest at Jantar Mantar. Officers cited alleged rule violations during an earlier demonstration by the group. Delhi Police sent a letter on October 9 to CJP co-convener Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna. Police said their communication on October 7 was not a proper application submitted 10 days in advance. Police also said Jantar Mantar has an official capacity to hold about 1,000 people at a time.

Authorities took major security measures across the city. Officials deployed 23,000 security personnel and closed 45 metro stations across Delhi. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs directed all States and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police. They were instructed to stop protesters from moving toward Delhi.

Security forces also made local detentions. NSUI Jamia Millia Islamia Secretary Ebin Basil reported that police detained four female students near Jamia around 11:30 p.m.. He said police released them around 3 a.m..

The Centre alleged that over 200 police personnel were injured during a CJP protest in July. Delhi Police said they identified 2,873 people using CCTV footage from a July 20 march. Police claimed 989 of those identified had criminal antecedents.

Despite the actions, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke urged supporters to continue. Dipke said on X that he would reach Delhi by 9:30 a.m.. He urged protesters to keep going even if he is detained.

Union Minister Chirag Paswan said the protesters are the youth of India and nobody can stop them. Paswan had previously called for clarification about Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's decision-making. But Paswan backed out after the Election Commission said decisions were unanimous.

In an open letter, 42 retired judges defended Gyanesh Kumar. They criticized the CJP-led protests against the Election Commission of India. Political protests against the commission have occurred before. In May 2014, the BJP staged protests against the Election Commission after candidate Narendra Modi was denied permission to hold a rally in Varanasi.

stories.headline: US suspends PERM green card processing for major technology companies
stories.body:
The Trump administration suspended eight major tech companies from the US PERM program on October 8. The affected firms include TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, and Capgemini. US Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced that authorities will stop accepting new applications and processing pending ones for these companies.

US Vice President JD Vance urged US companies to hire great American workers instead of foreign indentured servants. India's Ministry of External Affairs called Vance's comments deeply offensive and unwarranted. The ministry issued an official statement on October 9 regarding the immigration restrictions.

Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said talent mobility adds value to both the Indian and US economies. He said Indian talent helps US companies with cutting-edge work and job creation. The ministry noted that existing H-1B visas remain valid, though Indian nationals received 71 percent of all H-1B visas in the 2023-24 financial year.

Tata Consultancy Services said in a stock filing that it submitted fewer than 10 PERM applications over two years. It still plans to hire 15,000 US workers over five years. Pan IIT Alumni India Chairman Prabhat Kumar urged graduates to return to India, saying a visa was never a stable foundation.

US Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced that US authorities will stop accepting new applications and processing pending ones under the PERM program for the affected firms.
US Vice President JD Vance urged US companies to hire 'great American workers' instead of 'foreign indentured servants'.
India's Ministry of External Affairs called US Vice President JD Vance's comments deeply offensive and unwarranted.
India's Ministry of External Affairs issued an official statement on October 9 regarding the US immigration restrictions.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that talent mobility adds value to both the Indian and US economies and helps US companies with cutting-edge talent and job creation.
India's Ministry of External Affairs stated that the US PERM suspension does not advance shared ambitions and affects green card processing, though existing H-1B visas remain valid.
Indian nationals received 71% of all H-1B visas issued by the US in the 2023-24 financial year.
Tata Consultancy Services stated in a stock exchange filing that it submitted fewer than 10 PERM applications over the past two years and still plans to hire 15,000 US employees over five years.
Pan IIT Alumni India urged IIT graduates to return to India to work, citing uncertainty in US immigration policies.
PanIIT Alumni India Chairman Prabhat Kumar stated, 'A visa was never a stable foundation for a career... Build here. Scale here. Die here.'

stories.headline: Assembly and parliamentary bypoll election results declared across Indian states
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said recent bypoll election victories reflect public connection with the ruling coalition's agenda.

In Tamil Nadu, political party TVK won two assembly seats in Dharapuram and Madurantakam. Candidate P Sathyabama won Dharapuram by 9,471 votes, while Maragatham Kumaravel won Madurantakam by 20,040 votes. The wins increased TVK's total in the 234-member assembly from 107 to 109 seats.

In West Bengal, the BJP retained the Nandigram seat and won Rejinagar from AJUP. BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won Rejinagar with 1,29,914 votes, beating Golam Nabi Azad. In Nandigram, BJP's Hasirani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan by 1,22,753 votes.

In Assam, BJP candidate Devasish Sharma won the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat by over 1.5 lakh votes against AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. Following the loss, Raijor Dal chief Akhil Gogoi demanded the resignation of Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi. Gogoi said that Congress's minority vote share in Nagaon dropped from 25 percent to 5 percent. In Puducherry, AINRC candidate Ashok Anand won the Thattanchavady seat by over 8,400 votes.

claims.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the bypoll victories reflect the public's deep connection with the NDA's good governance agenda.
TVK won two assembly bypolls in Tamil Nadu, securing victories in Dharapuram and Madurantakam.
In Tamil Nadu, TVK's P Sathyabama won Dharapuram by 9,471 votes, and Maragatham Kumaravel won Madurantakam by 20,040 votes.
The bypoll wins increased TVK's tally in the 234-member Tamil Nadu assembly from 107 to 109 seats.
In West Bengal, the BJP retained the Nandigram assembly seat and won the Rejinagar assembly seat from AJUP.
Official Rejinagar bypoll results showed BJP's Shankharav Sarkar won with 1,29,914 votes while Azad received 54,098 votes.
In Nandigram, BJP's Hasirani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan by 1,22,753 votes.
In Assam, BJP's Devasish Sharma won the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, leading AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal by over 1.5 lakh votes.
Raijor Dal chief Akhil Gogoi demanded the resignation of Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi following the party's defeat in the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election.
Akhil Gogoi stated that Congress's minority vote share in Nagaon dropped from 25% to 5%.
AINRC candidate Ashok Anand won the Thattanchavady assembly bypoll in Puducherry by over 8,400 votes.
